target_customer: Data scientists and machine learning engineers who needed cloud GPUs to train deep learning models
problem: Setting up GPU machines, drivers and frameworks for deep learning was slow. FloydHub offered a command line tool that handled provisioning, running code and versioning results.
business_model: Usage-based cloud GPU platform with a hosted pay as you go model
product_category: Machine learning platform as a service

founders.name: Sai Prashanth Soundararaj
founders.background_notes: The YC launch post describes him as a former senior deep learning researcher at Microsoft.

founders.name: Naren Thiagarajan
founders.background_notes: The YC launch post describes him as formerly Director of Engineering at Avast.

exit.reason: Operations ended and users were pointed to NimbleBox for migration

competitors.name: Paperspace
competitors.what: Cloud computing with GPU capacity aimed at data scientists
competitors.traction_then: A three year old company when it launched GPU processing for data scientists

technical_complexity.rationale: GPU provisioning, environment setup and experiment versioning behind a simple command line were solid infrastructure work, but built on standard cloud GPUs.

defensibility.rationale: Stored experiment history created some lock-in, but the product sat on top of commodity cloud GPUs and larger clouds offered similar services.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large clouds and specialist GPU clouds served the same wedge. FloydHub shut down in August 2021.

market_need_then: Deep learning was growing quickly in 2016 and 2017, and the YC launch post cites about 500 deep learning hours run daily one week after launch and a planned Udacity partnership.

branding.domain_note: Used floydhub.com, an exact .com with a Hub suffix; the domain now redirects to blog.floydhub.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as Heroku for deep learning, per the YC launch post

branding.community_and_virality: Ran a company blog and a Product Hunt launch; the YC post cites a ProductHunt launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in the deep learning niche through its blog and Product Hunt launch, but a search for the name origin returned only Pink Floyd results and no brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: FloydHub launched in Winter 2017 as Heroku for deep learning and showed early usage, but specialist GPU clouds and the large cloud vendors served the same developers. It shut down in August 2021 and pointed users to NimbleBox, and the company has not published the reason. Competition and an inability to raise visible follow-on funding are inferred from the funding record and market, not stated by the company, so confidence in the factors is moderate.
notes: The floydhub.com homepage redirects to blog.floydhub.com and was not fetched further. Shutdown date of 2021-08-20 comes from a Dealroom style directory snippet and a July 2021 NimbleBox migration guide seen in search results. Whether NimbleBox acquired FloydHub is not established. Funding conflict: CB Insights reports about $120K total with Y Combinator, Bossa Invest, Amino Capital and Samsung NEXT as investors, while Dealroom alone shows a $4.0M seed with no date. Each of these rests on a single database. No Series A was found; an unrelated company called Floyd has a Series A listing. Paperspace source date is 2017-05, a few months after the batch. The 2016 launch name was Floyd and the rebrand date is not sourced.
